Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Anjani Kumar Mishra,J.
Hon'ble Ms. Nand Prabha Shukla,J.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned A.G.A. for the State.
The instant writ petition seeks quashing of the FIR dated 05.02.2023 giving rise to Case Crime No.93 of 2023, under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 I.P.C., Police Station- Cantt., District- Gorakhpur.
The contention of learned counsel for the petitioner is that he had in fact filed a Character Certificate issued on 13.02.2018.
Manipulation, if any, has been resorted to at the behest of his rivals.
No manipulation was made by the petitioner in the Character Certificate filed and relied upon by him.

sentences.text: The FIR alleges that a Character Certificate dated 13.07.2023 had been filed.
It is not in issue that the validity of a Character Certificate is three years.

It is submitted by learned AGA that the certificate furnished by the petitioner was, upon due inquiry conducted by the S.D.M. concerned, found to be a Character Certificate, which had never issued from the office of the District Magistrate.
Even otherwise, learned counsel for the petitioner is not in a position to state as to when and on what date he had used this Character Certificate allegedly dated 13.02.2018.
He has merely submitted that this certificate had been filed on numerous occasion for procuring various contracts.

Under the circumstances, this Court is constrained to hold that the submissions made by learned counsel for the petitioner are his defence, which cannot be looked into while dealing with a writ petition seeking quashing of the first information report.

Even otherwise, the allegations are such which necessarily require to be investigated and it is not possible for the writ court to rule in this regard especially because the issue being raised is a factual controversy beyond the scope of the writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
Moreover, the allegations in the FIR contain ingredients of a cognizable offence, which therefore,
Accordingly and in view of the above, the writ petition fails and is dismissed.
